name: Carrot Red
lede: Carrot red is a muted salmon-red; the name dates from the days when red carrots were grown.

sections.title: Carrots were not always orange
sections.body:
Paterson notes that carrots were not always orange: the Egyptians grew purple carrots from 2000 BC, the Romans ate purple and white ones, and red, black, green and yellow carrots also existed [1]. Dutch growers favored orange, which became the standard from around the sixteenth century [1]. The orange comes from beta-carotene [1].

The old name belongs to that earlier world: Paterson says carrot red dates from before the seventeenth century, when red carrots were grown, and the color now called carrot orange was formerly carrot red [1]. Compare [[orange]], [[coral]] and [[carmine]]. The dictionary also lists the adjective *carroty*, for anything reddish orange like the root [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch appears in 0.23% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (55 paintings, as photographed) [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 3.0 times the rate expected from the museums' baseline [2].

openers: Carrots were purple in ancient Egypt, and carrot red names the red ones.
